lines.trans: No matter how much I think about it, I wish I had never come here—our home was in Chuncheon, and I pestered my parents to bring me for my birthday.
After meeting CEO Byun, I practically lived in a Seoul practice room while my parents came up to Seoul every two weeks to see me.
Cindy, from now on I am your mother—just trust Mom and follow me.
If only I had not begged to come here that day, had never met CEO Byun, had never lived apart from Mom and Dad…
How wonderful would it have been if that accident had never happened that day?
Thinking it a hundred or a thousand times cannot change anything, yet I thought it every single night for ten years—and could never fall asleep.
It is not your fault, Ms. Cindy—your parents would never think that either, and they would want you to stop asking "what if" now.
Instead, they would tell you that you have done wonderfully all on your own and worked so hard.
Could you hold my hand? I thought I would never set foot here again in my life—I am really glad I came today.
From now on, whenever someone mentions an amusement park, I think I will remember you, Producer.
Me?

meanings.note: Used as numeral + counter (10년).

examples.text: 사흘만 신세 질게요. 연습생 시작하고 10년 동안 나 하루도 쉬어본 적이 없어요.
examples.trans: Let me impose on you for just three days—in the ten years since starting as a trainee, I have never rested a single day.
For the first time in ten years, I am eating a home-cooked meal on my birthday.

meanings.note: Used as numeral + counter + -에 (2주에).

examples.text: 변 대표님 만난 다음부터는 서울에 있는 연습실에서 살다시피 했어요. 부모님이 2주에 한 번씩 나 보러 서울에 다녀가셨고.
examples.trans: After meeting CEO Byun, I practically lived in a Seoul practice room while my parents came up to Seoul every two weeks to see me.
This point about every two weeks is really important.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: refers to a previously mentioned or specific day

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
I don't have time that day.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used as compound noun (놀이공원).

examples.text: 놀이공원 측에서 연락 왔는데요, 야외 취침할 장소 포인트는 직접 보셨으면 하던데요.
examples.trans: The amusement park contacted us—they hoped you would inspect the outdoor sleeping spot in person.

examples.text: 13살에 놀이공원만 안 갔어도! 나 13살에 데뷔해서 뭘 아냐고!
examples.trans: If only I had never gone to that amusement park at thirteen! What could a thirteen-year-old debuting possibly know?!

meanings.note: Used as honorific past + -고 (다녀가셨고.).

examples.text: 변 대표님 만난 다음부터는 서울에 있는 연습실에서 살다시피 했어요. 부모님이 2주에 한 번씩 나 보러 서울에 다녀가셨고.
examples.trans: After meeting CEO Byun, I practically lived in a Seoul practice room while my parents came up to Seoul every two weeks to see me.
Let us do that (visited and headed back) right away.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Used after a time period.

examples.trans: for three days
for three days (2)

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.en: to follow, to come along behind
meanings.note: Compound of 따르다 ('to follow') + 오다 ('to come').

examples.trans: Follow me.
Follow me this way.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 만약에 기억을 하는데도 아무 반응을 안 보이고 있는 거라면, 준모가 그 진심을 편집해버렸단 얘기 아닐까?
examples.trans: If he remembers everything and still shows no reaction, does that not mean Joon-mo edited out those feelings?
Here the word for 'if by chance' is key.

meanings.note: Used both as an adverb and a noun

examples.trans: I drink coffee every morning.
I try to exercise every day.

meanings.note: Used as connective -고 (믿고).

examples.text: 신디야, 이제 내가 네 엄마야. 엄마만 믿고 따라오면 돼.
examples.trans: Cindy, from now on I am your mother—just trust Mom and follow me.
Let us do that (trusting and) right away.
I want to worth hoping for right now.
How about trying to worth hoping for together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'nights' is key.

meanings.note: Used as Sino-Korean numeral (백).

examples.text: 아니, 내가 아까 백 번 설명할 땐 이해한다고 그러더니 지금 또 이게 무슨 망언이야?
examples.trans: Wait—when I explained it a hundred times earlier you said you understood, so what outrageous remark is this now?

examples.text: 우리 엄마는 영화배우 장국영 좋아했는데 아빠가 장국영이 광고하는 초콜릿 백 개씩 사다 바쳐야 엄마랑 사귈 수 있었대요.
examples.trans: My mom loved actor Leslie Cheung, and she said my dad had to bring her a hundred chocolates from his commercials just to date her.

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 혼자서 자유로운 싱글의 삶을 누려보려고 부모님한테 어렵게 얻어낸 집인데,
examples.trans: I worked so hard to talk my parents into getting this place so I could enjoy a free single life alone…
Here the word for 'from my parents' is key.

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.
I live in Seoul.
Where do you live?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 사는데요, 삽니다)
noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

meanings.note: Used as causal -아서 (생각나서).

examples.text: 저희 어머님은 가수 전영록 씨 노래를 들으면 아직도 옛날 연애하던 좋았던 시절이 생각나서 가슴이 떨리고 좋으시답니다.
examples.trans: Whenever my mother hears singer Jeon Young-rok's songs, her heart still flutters happily remembering the sweet days when she was young and in love.

examples.text: 이제는 놀이공원 하면 피디님 생각날 것 같아.
examples.trans: From now on, whenever someone mentions an amusement park, I think I will remember you, Producer.
Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.

meanings.note: Used as noun + exclamatory copula (생일이네!).

examples.trans: Really? Today is your birthday! Happy day you were born!

examples.text: 그걸 내가 알았니? 준모야, 우리 저녁에 신디 생일 파티 해주자!
examples.trans: How was I supposed to know?! Joon-mo, let us throw Cindy a birthday party tonight!

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.en: to work hard, put in effort
meanings.note: 수고하셨습니다 is the standard workplace phrase for 'good work / thank you for your hard work'

examples.trans: Good work today as well!
You really worked hard.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used as adverb (아무리).

examples.text: 아무리 생각해도 여기 오지 않았으면 좋았을 것 같아요. 우리 집 춘천이었는데 그날 내 생일이라고 졸라서 여기 온 거고.
examples.trans: No matter how much I think about it, I wish I had never come here—our home was in Chuncheon, and I pestered my parents to bring me for my birthday.
I thought it over again (no matter how much).

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 우리 아빠가 은행에서 퇴직하시고 사업하셨다가 망하는 바람에 집을 헐값에 내놨는데,
examples.trans: After my dad retired from the bank and his business went under, we had to put the apartment up dirt cheap.
Here the word for 'dad' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.en: how much / how many / how long
meanings.note: Asks about degree, amount, price, or duration

examples.trans: How much will the repair cost be?
How long does it take from here to the station?

meanings.note: affectionate/informal word for mother

examples.trans: I went to the market with my mum.
The food my mum makes is the most delicious.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Used as noun (연습실).

examples.text: 우리 신디 다 컸네, 연습실 한구석에서 엄마 보고 싶다고 집에 가고 싶다고 울던 애가.
examples.trans: Our Cindy is all grown up—the girl who used to cry in a corner of the practice room wanting her mom and home.

examples.text: 변 대표님 만난 다음부터는 서울에 있는 연습실에서 살다시피 했어요. 부모님이 2주에 한 번씩 나 보러 서울에 다녀가셨고.
examples.trans: After meeting CEO Byun, I practically lived in a Seoul practice room while my parents came up to Seoul every two weeks to see me.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
I understand well (on the contrary).
Today is a (on the contrary) busy day.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그냥 어제를 내 인생에서 확 도려내버리고 싶다.
examples.trans: I just want to carve yesterday right out of my life.
Here the word for 'from my life' is key.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 자꾸 잘못 읽으니까 그렇지, 읽지 마!
examples.trans: That is because you keep reading it wrong—do not read between the lines!
Here the word for 'wrongly' is key.

meanings.note: verb do well

examples.trans: Study well.
You did well.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 저도 밖에서는 잠을 잘 못 자서요, 이것저것 준비했거든요.
examples.trans: Since I cannot sleep well outdoors either, I prepared a few things.
Here the word for 'sleep' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 일주일에 스케줄 22개 잡아준 대표님도 독하고 버텨내는 너도 독하다.
examples.trans: The CEO is ruthless for booking twenty-two events in one week, and you are just as tough for enduring it.
This expression comes from 'booked'.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used as causal -아서 (졸라서).

examples.text: 아무리 생각해도 여기 오지 않았으면 좋았을 것 같아요. 우리 집 춘천이었는데 그날 내 생일이라고 졸라서 여기 온 거고.
examples.trans: No matter how much I think about it, I wish I had never come here—our home was in Chuncheon, and I pestered my parents to bring me for my birthday.

examples.text: 내가 그날 여기 오자고 조르지만 않았으면, 변 대표를 만나지 않았으면, 엄마 아빠랑 헤어져서 살지 않았으면…
examples.trans: If only I had not begged to come here that day, had never met CEO Byun, had never lived apart from Mom and Dad…
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.trans: The food is really delicious today.
Time really flies.

meanings.note: Used as numeral (천).

examples.text: 백 번 천 번 생각한다고 그렇게 될 수 있는 것도 아닌데 난 10년 동안 매일 밤 그 생각을 했어요. 그 생각만 하면 잠이 안 왔어.
examples.trans: Thinking it a hundred or a thousand times cannot change anything, yet I thought it every single night for ten years—and could never fall asleep.
This point about a thousand is really important.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour
I want to let's break up right now.
How about trying to let's break up together tomorrow?
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun
